paras: The attempted lynching of Bob Baker and King Lyons was a mob's failed attempt in August 1915 to take two Black men accused of murdering a white sawmill owner from the Concordia parish jail at Vidalia, Louisiana. Sheriff Eugene Campbell refused a decoy call meant to draw him away and rowed the prisoners across the Mississippi River to Natchez before the mob could reach them. Mississippi papers reported the episode as a mob foiled by the sheriff.

Walter Zimmerman, a sawmill owner near Fish Pond who had come from Danville, Illinois, was killed on August 12, 1915, and his body was found in the woods with gunshot wounds. A first Natchez item called his death a mystery, describing him as a recluse with no known enemies. By August 14, Baker, his wife, and Lyons, all employed by Zimmerman, were in jail at Vidalia, and according to the coroner Baker had confessed to killing him to rob him.

The wires differed on who was implicated: one said both men confessed, the Evening Star said Baker named his wife and Lyons, and a later item named only Lyons. A special guard was placed at the Vidalia jail because the killing was "reported to have aroused high feeling against the negroes."

According to a Natchez dispatch dated August 24, the mob first tried to get the sheriff out of the way with a message that a murder had been committed in a remote part of the parish. Campbell suspected a trick and refused to go. Instead he hurried the prisoners from the jail to a skiff and rowed across the river "last night," foiling "a mob attempting to force the jail."

At Natchez the prisoners were held overnight in the Adams county jail. The sheriff then left with them, by one account on Monday morning for "parts unknown" and by another for a place that was "supposedly Tallulah." The August 24 dispatch counted Baker's wife among the prisoners, while the state-news item named only the two men.
No arrests of mob members, and no trial or later outcome for the accused, appear in the coverage.

Outside Mississippi the case appeared only as a brief murder story, under headlines such as "Two Confess to Murder" in the South Bend News-Times and "Three Held in Murder Case" in the Washington Evening Star. The Hattiesburg News ran the jail attempt on August 24 as "Mob's Trick Fails." A separate state-news item followed from August 27, headed "Mob Was Foiled" in the Greenwood Commonwealth and the Macon Beacon and placed among "Mississippi State Briefs" in the Brookhaven and Rosedale papers.

Both versions credited the sheriff and presented the confessions as settled, and the state-news item called the murder "cold blooded and brutal." The same item also said that after $20 was found in Baker's hat band, "the officers forced him to tell the details." No coverage of the episode in the Black press was found.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Bob Baker and King Lyons
bases: Two Natchez reports describe a mob's attempt to lynch Black prisoners accused of murder, foiled when the sheriff removed them from the Concordia parish jail (A4, A7).

No one was killed: the sheriff took the prisoners across the river before the mob reached them (A4, A7); the mob acted on the murder accusation, but its size is not given, so this was an attempted, not a completed, lynching.

Two differently worded Natchez reports, a dated dispatch (A4) and a state-news item (A6, A7), agree on the sheriff, the decoy message and the escape by skiff, and Aug. 14 wires confirm the arrests and the guard at the jail (A1, A2).

accounts.label: Natchez wire, Aug. 14
accounts.gist: Baker and Lyons (with Baker's wife in one version) were jailed at Vidalia after Zimmerman's body was found; a special guard was placed at the jail because of high feeling.

accounts.label: Natchez dispatch, Aug. 24
accounts.gist: A mob tried to trick the sheriff away and then to force the Concordia jail; the sheriff rowed Baker, his wife and Lyons across the river to Natchez and took them on to 'parts unknown'.

accounts.label: Natchez state-news item
accounts.gist: Sheriff Campbell frustrated an attempt to lynch Baker and Lyons, ignoring a decoy telephone call, and took them by skiff to Natchez and then 'supposedly' to Tallulah.

framing.detail: Mississippi papers ran the attempt as 'Mob's Trick Fails' and 'Mob Was Foiled', crediting the sheriff while calling the murder 'cold blooded and brutal' and treating the confessions as settled.
Northern dailies carried only the murder-and-confession wire ('Two Confess to Murder', 'Three Held in Murder Case'), not the lynching attempt.
